log.text: Tsareena used High Jump Kick → Rotom

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott + Delphox to deny Aerodactyl’s Tailwind while pressuring Metagross without relying on rain. Preserve Tsareena as the strongest Rotom-Wash answer, with Basculegion providing priority and late-game cleanup once Rotom is controlled.
decisions.notebook: Opponent uses Aerodactyl as post-KO speed control and Rotom-Wash as the primary answer to the rain core; under opposing Tailwind, Rotom outspeeds 143-Speed Basculegion and attacks freely without Protect. Incineroar supports that endgame with Intimidate and sustained Flare Blitz pressure. Preserve Tsareena for Rotom-Wash, prioritize denying Aerodactyl’s Tailwind, and avoid plans whose only durable damage route is Basculegion. A non-rain Delphox mode offers immediate Metagross pressure while keeping Tsareena and Basculegion for cleanup.

decisions.rationale: G1 plan won; keep identical bring and lead. Incineroar Fake Out + Intimidate disrupts Whimsicott/Basculegion openers, Mega Metagross pressures; Aerodactyl (200 Spe) is Tailwind/Wide Guard backup once Whimsicott dies; Rotom-W walls Politoed rain and answers Mudsdale if brought. Incineroar preserved as Last Respects switch-in and Delphox wall.
decisions.notebook: G1 WON with Incineroar/Mega Metagross/Aerodactyl/Rotom-W vs Whimsicott/Basculegion/Politoed/Tsareena (Delphox+Mudsdale not brought). G2: same four, lead Incin+Metagross. Coverage: Mudsdale (Inner Focus ignores Fake Out+Intimidate → Rotom Hydro Pump/Aerodactyl); Mega Delphox (max 204 Spe; Incin walls Heat Wave/Shadow Ball/Grass Knot — preserve Incin). Foe plan: Whimsicott (Prankster/Sash) Tailwind → Basculegion snowball; Politoed Helping Hand support (seen on Aqua Jet). Whimsicott is their ONLY Tailwind — kill early, then Aerodactyl (200) owns speed (only max Mega Delphox outspeeds); Tailwind applies the turn used. Basculegion: Adaptability Life Orb Jolly, HAS Protect — Protects vs predicted double-targets, so hit the partner those turns. Last Respects = 50+50 per fainted ally (BP150 with 2; tools show 50 — trust this note): OHKOs Metagross from 50%, Rotom from full; Incin (Dark) resists = the Last Respects switch-in. Wave Crash OHKOs Incin even at -1 without rain — never leave Incin exposed. Ghost: Fake Out immune, Bullet Punch resisted. Rotom (118) slower than Jolly Basc (143) — Thunderbolt 58-106% is Tailwind/revenge-only; pair with Flare Blitz chip (resisted, 20-38%). Politoed: Drizzle/Sitrus/Calm, Weather Ball/Icy Wind/Helping Hand/Protect = support. Rain Weather Ball 61-139% vs Incin (never switch Incin in); Rotom walls it, Thunderbolt 51.8-90.9% vs Calm+Sitrus needs chip. Rain halves Flare Blitz; rain self-expires in 5 turns (died turn 6 G1) — stalling/sacking drains it, but Drizzle resets on switch-in so don't assume it's gone.

decisions.rationale: Tailwind plus Mega Heat Wave creates a Fake Out fork: if Delphox is stopped, speed control is established; if Whimsicott is stopped, Mega Delphox pressures Metagross heavily while chipping Incineroar. This avoids exposing Tsareena, the key Rotom-Wash answer, and prepares Basculegion for later cleanup.

decisions.rationale: Shadow Ball safely finishes Metagross before it can act, while Wave Crash threatens a guaranteed KO on Incineroar and Basculegion outspeeds it. This creates immediate double-KO pressure without Heat Wave’s miss risk and punishes Incineroar for staying instead of pivoting.

Metagross (156) is outsped by Delphox (169+) and dies to Heat Wave before moving, so fire guaranteed priority Bullet Punch into Basculegion (chip pushes it into Rotom Thunderbolt KO range), then sack it for a free Aerodactyl entry. Incineroar is OHKOed by Wave Crash (Basc has no Intimidate drop) and is too slow to Parting Shot, so hard-switch to Rotom-Wash, which resists Wave Crash (21.7-59.2% pre-Adaptability, survives). Next turn: Rock Slide + Thunderbolt double Basculegion; Rotom and Aerodact

decisions.rationale: Only decision is Metagross's replacement. Incineroar cannot enter vs Basculegion: Wave Crash OHKOs it even at -1, and Aqua Jet/Last Respects pressure remains. Aerodactyl (200 Spe, Focus Sash) outspeeds Basculegion guaranteed, threatens Rock Slide (2x SE on Delphox, chips both), Wide Guard blocks Heat Wave, Tailwind available. Sash covers the max-Speed Delphox case. Incin stays preserved as the Delphox answer for after Basculegion falls.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Rotom: priority Aqua Jet plus Grass Knot secures the KO even against heavy bulk before Rotom can act. Delphox is guaranteed faster than Aerodactyl, so both attacks land before Tailwind. Aerodactyl may establish speed control, but removing the main Basculegion answer creates a favorable 3v2 endgame.
decisions.notebook: Aerodactyl is the opponent’s post-KO Tailwind setter; deny Tailwind when practical, but prioritize removing Rotom-Wash when both cannot be stopped. Rotom-Wash is the primary rain-core answer and may be specially bulky enough to survive Grass Knot alone; combine chip with Grass Knot when a guaranteed removal is needed. Incineroar supports the endgame through Intimidate, Fake Out, and Flare Blitz. Preserve Tsareena to pressure Rotom-Wash and use Queenly Majesty to block Incineroar’s Fake Out during Tailwind turns. Delphox-Mega is guaranteed faster than unboosted Jolly Aerodactyl and provides immediate pressure into Steel-heavy leads.

Tailwind applies immediately, so Rotom (236) outspeeds even max-Speed Basculegion (143), eliminating the Last Respects KO risk on Rotom; Thunderbolt is a guaranteed KO on Basc at 54% (58.1-105.6%). decisions.rationale: Protect preserves Delphox from fast Hydro Pump/Rock Slide while Tsareena removes Rotom. High Jump Kick is more accurate than Power Whip, still guarantees the KO from the shown range, and better punishes a Volt Switch into Incineroar.

Rotom sacks itself burning the only real threat; I keep a 3v2 with Incin walling Delphox and Aero free to re-enter under Tailwind.

Protect shields Tsareena from a likely lethal Flare Blitz while Delphox uses its strongest accurate single-target attack into Aerodactyl. This avoids Wide Guard and starts removing the foe controlling speed; attacking with burned, -1 Tsareena is too weak and risks losing it before it moves.

Queenly Majesty blocks Fake Out vs both foes, so skip it. Rock Slide chips Delphox 42-97% (into next-turn Slide KO range) with 30% flinch on each foe; Flare Blitz + Slide chip KOs burned Tsareena, removing the only HJK threat. Burned -1 HJK does ~18-38% to Incin; Delphox can't hurt either mon. Even double Protect just delays a turn.

Mudsdale Inner Focus ignores Fake Out/Intimidate. Tsareena Queenly Majesty blocks ALL opposing priority targeting it OR its ally (Fake Out/Bullet Punch useless while it's up). Triple Axel multi-hit bypasses Sash — never rely on Sash vs Tsareena. Delphox raw Spe up to 204 > Aero 200 outside Tailwind, but Delphox can't KO Aero (Heat Wave 18-37%) and Incin walls it. Endgame: Rock Slide spam Delphox during Tailwind, Incin pivots/Parting Shot; sack low-HP mons for free entries. Whimsicott (their only Tailwind) and Basculegion dead; Politoed walled by Rotom if seen G3.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Double Protect is the only line that can preserve both Pokémon through the final Tailwind turn. Tsareena otherwise moves after Incineroar and is KOed by Flare Blitz before acting, while Delphox is exposed to Rock Slide. Although Tsareena’s repeat Protect is only partially reliable, success lets both outspeed the foes once Tailwind expires.

decisions.rationale: Rock Slide guarantees the KO on Delphox from 19% (41.8-96.7% range) and chips Tsareena 17-38%; Flare Blitz then does 74-165% to Tsareena, so combined damage (90-203%) is a near-certain KO. Both foes falling this turn ends the game (their other two are dead) and the series 2-0. Only Protect/miss saves them, and Tsareena's Protect is reduced; even then we win the ensuing endgame since Delphox can't break Incineroar and Aero outspeeds Tsareena even after Tailwind ends.

reflections.summary: The four were too dependent on Basculegion to control Incineroar. After Rotom-Wash removed Basculegion and the Intimidate plus Will-O-Wisp sequence neutralized Tsareena, Aerodactyl’s Tailwind and Incineroar’s repeated Flare Blitzes controlled the endgame. Mega Delphox suited Metagross and unboosted Aerodactyl, but could not carry the resulting Aerodactyl/Incineroar matchup alone.
reflections.adjustment: At team preview, keep Mega Delphox only with a plan to preserve Whimsicott until Aerodactyl appears: use Prankster Taunt to deny Tailwind and preserve Basculegion as the late-game Incineroar answer rather than trading it into Rotom-Wash.
reflections.notebook: Opponent uses Intimidate plus Rotom-Wash Will-O-Wisp to neutralize Tsareena, then pressures it with Incineroar’s Flare Blitz. Preserve Whimsicott to Taunt Aerodactyl when it enters after a KO. Preserve Basculegion for Incineroar; Rotom-Wash can survive the initial combined chip and retaliate. Mega Delphox is appropriate into Metagross and outspeeds unboosted Aerodactyl, but requires prior Aerodactyl chip or multiple attacks to finish it.

reflections.summary: Won because the opponent reran the exact same four as G1 (Whimsicott/Basculegion/Mega Delphox/Tsareena) into a prepared counter-plan: Intimidate + Will-O-Wisp neutered Tsareena, Rotom traded up into Basculegion, Aerodactyl's same-turn Tailwind seized speed control, and the endgame double-target on 19% Mega Delphox was guaranteed — the resisted Flare Blitz KO'd even after Rock Slide missed. Zero decision errors; the team-preview plan (Incineroar pivot + Aero/Rotom + Mega Metagross) fully matched
reflections.adjustment: Metagross-Mega was sacrificed early and contributed nothing visible — the Aerodactyl/Rotom/Incineroar core beats their repeated four by itself. reflections.notebook: Series won 2-0 (I'm p2).
